To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electronic modification of the PYA ligands allows for the fine-tuning of the catalytic properties of iridium complexes.
the electronic properties of PYA ligands can be tuned by the introduction of donor substituants in the phenyl ring.

a facile modification of the C,N-chelate pyridylidenerhodamine ligand by the incorporation of methoxy substituents in different positions of its aryl ring results in an enhanced catalytic performance of the corresponding iridium complexes toward carbonyl reduction.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the synthesis of new iridium catalysts based on PYA ligands, the electronic tuning of the iridium center by the PYA ligand and the catalytic activity toward transfer hydrogenation of imines and carbonyls as well as hydrosilylations.

the design of a novel family of PYA ligands with variable electronic and steric properties, and the application of this family as a modular tool for the synthesis of a series of iridium catalysts with different catalytic properties.
the development of new iridium(III) complexes based on C,N-bidentates with variable donor properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the electronic modification of the PYA ligand by the incorporation of electron-donating substituents at the phenyl ring increases the catalytic activity for the reduction of carbonyl compounds and imines, whereas the base-free reduction of aldehydes is not significantly enhanced.
the electronic modification of the C,N-chelating PYA ligand at iridium is a powerful tool for tuning the reactivity and the catalytic activity in transfer hydrogenation and related reactions.

the electronic properties of the PYA ligand have a strong influence on the catalytic activity and selectivity of the corresponding iridium complex, which is reflected by a change from an electron-deficient iridium complex with a low catalytic activity to an electron-rich iridium center with a high catalytic activity and an excellent chemoselectivity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of the PYA ligand family in iridium catalysis provides access to a broad variety of catalytic transformations with a single catalyst precursor.
the catalytic activity and the selectivity can be fine-tuned by the introduction of donor substituets at the PYA ligand.
the electronic modification of the PYA iridum(III) complexes allows for a fine-tuning of their activity and selectivity in catalytic reactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electronic properties of the ligand can easily be tuned to optimize the catalytic activity toward different reactions.
the PYA iridum(III) complexes with methoxy-substituted PYA ligands are excellent catalyst precursors for the transfer hydrogenation of imines, aldehydes, ketones, and phenylacetylenes.
the catalytic activity is strongly dependent on the donor properties of the ligand, which is reflected in the redox potentials and the catalytic turnover numbers (TONs) of the complexes.
